source_text: Non ante anima Verbo iungitur nisi omnis hiems perturbationum vitiorumque procella discesserit, ut ultra non fluctuat et circumferatur omni vento doctrinae. Ubi haec discesserint, flores virtutum vernant et tempus putationis advenit, ut superfluum reseceatur ad gemmas spiritalis intelligentiae.
pass_a_gloss: Not before soul to-Word is-joined unless every winter of-disturbances and-of-vices storm has-departed, that further not she-may-surge and be-carried-about by-every wind of-teaching. Where these have-departed, flowers of-virtues spring and time of-pruning arrives, that superfluous may-be-cut-back toward buds of-spiritual understanding.
pass_b_english: The soul is not joined to the Word until every winter of disturbances and the storm of vices has departed, so that she no longer surges and is [[carried about by every wind of teaching >> Bible:Ephesians 4:14]]. When these have gone, flowers of the virtues spring up and [[the time of pruning >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:12]] comes, that the superfluous may be cut back toward buds of spiritual understanding.
